Why do people always post archive links in the comments? Seems to defeat the purpose really as I mostly find out about them after reading the article.

Good question! I archive in the comments for a few reasons. Personally I don't care about archiving the news sites I follow because I figure if a news site is bad enough to archive, I might as well just drop them as a source and find someone else. But not everyone feels the same way about every news source, and archiving is just a small courtesy for people who choose not to support my choice of source.

Additionally, archiving provides access to content that might be firewalled or region-locked, in which case a reader might not know they can't access something until after they've tried.

Lastly, posting the source link as a post and archiving in the comments means that the source domain shows up next to the post before you click; archiving the post and commenting the source just makes the domain say "archive.is". Since most voaters are in the habit of checking the comments when they need an archive, I've gotten into the habit of archiving my own posts as a courtesy.
Quite a reply. Thanks. Seems like I need to develop the habit as well.

No problem! And it's not something I want to force on others to do, but it's an extra courtesy when you've got extra time and wish to. If you do frequently archive your posts, check out this bookmarklet I posted over in /v/Efficiency; it will grab the URL of a current page, queue voat's "share a link" page in a new tab - pre-filled with the source URL - and create an archive.is link in the original tab, ready to copy/paste as soon as your post is submitted.
